findings.issue: The exact-keys guard does not reject an options variable that carries only bot keys (no advice key). D-4 says the guard rejects a bot's style or parameters 'for literals and for variables', and REQ-035.3 wants that to be a compile error. Because O is constrained `extends RecommendOptions` (an all-optional weak type), a variable such as `{ style: TAG_STYLE }` or `{ random: botRandom(1) }` fails the constraint, so inference falls back to O = RecommendOptions. ExactOptions<RecommendOptions, RecommendOptions> is `RecommendOptions & Record<never, never>`, and that intersection is not checked as a weak type, so the variable is accepted. The SPEC-08 literal `{ style: 'Maniac' }` is only rejected by the excess-property check after that same fallback, not by ExactOptions. recommendPostflop (postflop.ts:62) and gradeView (grade.ts:144) have the same gap.
findings.evidence: Scratch tsc project (/tmp/t75check, extends the repo tsconfig). These compile with no error: `const styleOnly = { style: 'Rock' }; recommend(view, styleOnly);`, `const r = { random: botRandom(1) }; recommend(view, r); gradeView(view, 'call', r);`, `const extra = { random: 1 } as const; recommend(view, { ...extra });`. These are correctly rejected: `recommend(view, maniacOptions)`, `gradeView(view, 'call', stationOptions)`, `recommendPostflop(view, stationOptions)`, and a variable `{ style: 'Maniac', equity: undefined }`.
findings.fix: Loosen the constraint so inference keeps the caller's keys, and intersect with Allowed so the value types are still checked: `export type ExactOptions<O, Allowed> = O & Allowed & Readonly<Record<Exclude<keyof O, keyof Allowed>, never>>;` with `<O extends object = RecommendOptions>` on recommend and gradeView, and `<O extends object = PostflopOptions>` on recommendPostflop. Verified in the scratch project: this rejects `{style}` and `{random}` variables, CallingStationOptions, and `{ equity: 5 }`. It still accepts `RecommendOptions | undefined` (the tag-playtest mock signature), `{ opponentRanges: 'actions' }`, no argument, and spreads of RecommendOptions. Add one `@ts-expect-error` line to a non-locked test, e.g. tests/advice/ranges.test.ts: `const styleOnly = { style: TAG_STYLE }; recommend(view, styleOnly)`. Explicit type arguments (`recommend<RecommendOptions>(view, x)`) and variables already widened to RecommendOptions can't be caught structurally. That is acceptable, but say so in the ExactOptions doc comment.

findings.issue: §5 Draw (b) requires at least one of the four run ranks to come from a hole card. No test catches it if that condition is dropped.
findings.evidence: Mutation in a scratch copy: removing `&& run.some((x) => fromHole.has(x))` from hasOpenEnder (ranges.ts:316) left every test in range-model.acceptance, ranges and postflop-ranges green.
findings.fix: Add a classifier case where the 4-run is all on the board, e.g. `classify('Ah Kd', '5c 6d 7h 8s')` → 'air'. A K on a 5-6-7-8 turn board makes no pair and no flush draw.

findings.issue: D-3 orders street aggregation as raise > bet > call > check. The aggregation test only covers bet beating call. No test catches swapping raise and bet, which matters when an opponent bets and then re-raises on the same street.
findings.evidence: Mutation in a scratch copy: AGGRESSION = ['bet', 'raise', 'call', 'check'] left all new tests green. Using the last action instead (['call', 'check', 'raise', 'bet']) is caught.
findings.fix: In 'expands, narrows per street and estimates from the view', assert the hero-3 check-raise line from seat 6's view: estimateOpponentRanges(viewOf(flop, 6))[0].combos equals narrowRange(start, flop board, 'raise'). Or add a bet / raise / re-raise street and assert 'raise' narrowing.

summary: The implementation matches the spec on substance. The classifier passes every §5/SPEC-10 edge case, including a paired or trips board, a straight on the board, A234 and JQKA, and a 4-flush with no hole card. Preflop lines, including limps, 3-bets, 4-bets and all-in blinds, follow A-4. Dead-card expansion, the A-5 empty-narrowing guard, the A-6 fallback chain and A-3 heads-up starts all match. The service, review and Table.tsx use ACTION_RANGE_ADVICE. Mutation checks show these tests catch real regressions: reverting the service recommend or grade, or userReviewEntries; allowing JQKA; last-action aggregation; dropping the empty guard; dropping the start fallback; a flush draw with no hole card; >= instead of > boardCat; and no blocked-start fallback. Bots are unchanged: adviceOptions drops only keys the engine never read, and the playtest SHA reproduced as 442dbf55...8fbc with 0 invariant violations. Test speed is fine: the property test ran in 0.88 s uncontended and the default-advice test in 0.95 s, far below the 10 s CI limit. One MAJOR: the AC#8 exact-keys guard is bypassed by an options variable that holds only bot keys ({style} or {random}). A fix has been verified. Two MINOR test-strength gaps.
